Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

text:
This looks like early 2009, most likely February or March. The 12-month equity drawdown of -47% and a 6-month return of -41.7% fit the trough in March 2009, and the other figures point the same way.

- **Equities:** the S&P was down about 11% in February 2009 and about 8% in January. The 1-month return of -15.4% is steeper than either, though it could match a February reading with some rounding and index differences. Measured over the period through February 2009, the 12-month return was about -43%, which is close to the -44.7% shown.
- **Labor market:** unemployment of 7.6% matches January/February 2009, when the rate was 7.6% in January and 7.8% in February. Payrolls averaging -590k over three months also fit January 2009.
- **Inflation:** headline CPI of -0.15% year over year matches March 2009 (-0.4%) or February (+0.2%). January was 0.0%. The reading is roughly -0.15%, which suggests February or March.
- **Fed funds and VIX:** a fed funds rate of 0.22% fits the 2009 period. A VIX of 44.66 fits February 2009 (about 44.8 at the end of the month).
- **Yields:** the 10-year yield of 2.98% and the 2-year yield of 1.08% match end-February 2009.

Unemployment of 7.6% would be the January 2009 value, which is published in early February. The data are "latest published," so end-of-February would show 7.6% for January, since the February figure comes out in early March. CPI for January 2009 was 0.0% year over year, and the stated -0.15% is close to that. End-February 2009 fits best.
